turns.assessment: The simultaneous OSC loss in both directions on the S20–S01 and S20–S13 routes, together with downstream amplifier input LOS, localizes the event to the fibre plant immediately adjacent to S20. The identical onset across both cables strongly indicates one excavation/common-duct event cutting multiple fibres, rather than amplifier, transceiver, WSS, or OTN-switch failure; unchanged pump currents and unaffected optical instrumentation elsewhere reinforce this.

proposals.rationale: This first span out of S20 reports OSC_LOS at the common onset, while the reverse terminal span also loses OSC. The S20–S13 cable fails simultaneously in the same way, consistent with the documented behavior of an excavation cutting both fibres and additional cables sharing the duct near S20. This isolates S20 and interrupts svc298's dependent working transport.
A sufficiently large loss increase can lose both payload and OSC, but simultaneous hard loss on both directions of two separate routes is much more characteristic of a common-duct cut.
S20 is common to the affected working paths, but a WSS input-port failure would not explain bidirectional OSC loss on two fibre routes.
